auth.description: An Algolia API key with the ACLs this connector needs: `search` and `browse` for the reads, `addObject` and `deleteObject` for the writes. Scope it to the indices this connection should reach rather than using the Admin key
auth.name: algolia.api_key
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: Create one under API Keys in the Algolia dashboard, with the search, browse, addObject and deleteObject ACLs restricted to the indices this connection should reach. Algolia shows the full key in the dashboard; the Admin key is deliberately not what this asks for
config.label: Algolia API key
config.name: api_key

config.help: The ten-character application id shown at the top of the API Keys page in your Algolia dashboard, e.g. B1G2GM9NG0. It identifies your Algolia application, forms the hostname every call goes to, and is sent as a header on every request — you supply it once here and this connector puts it in both places. It is not a secret; Algolia publishes it in client-side code
config.label: Algolia application id
config.name: app_id

description: Algolia search: list an application's indices, search one, and read, save or delete a single record by its object id

operations.description: List the indices in this Algolia application, with each index's record count and size. This is the call that discovers the index names every other operation here takes

dataSize.description: The size of the index's records in bytes

entries.description: How many records the index holds

fileSize.description: The size of the index on disk in bytes, records plus internal structures

lastBuildTimeS.description: How long the index's last build took, in seconds

name.description: The index name — what every other operation here passes as `index_name`

numberOfPendingTasks.description: Indexing operations accepted but not yet applied. Non-zero means a recent write is not visible to search yet

pendingTask.description: Whether any indexing operation is still pending

primary.description: For a replica index, the name of the index it replicates. Absent on a primary

replicas.description: The names of this index's replicas, if it has any

nbPages.description: How many pages of indices exist. This connector requests only the first

operations.description: Search one index and return the matching records. Algolia ranks results by its own configured relevance, so the order is the index's, not this connector's; `hits_per_page` and `page` walk the result set, and `filters` narrows it with Algolia's filter syntax over the index's own attributes

params.description: The index to search, from algolia-index-list's `name` field
params.name: index_name

params.description: The search text. An empty string matches every record in the index, ranked by the index's own ranking rules — which is how this operation browses rather than searches
params.name: query

params.description: How many records to return per page. Algolia's own default is 20 and its maximum is 1000
params.name: hits_per_page

params.description: Which page of results to return, counting from 0
params.name: page

params.description: An Algolia filter expression over this index's own attributes, e.g. `category:book AND price < 20`. The attribute names are the index's content and are not knowable here; an index that has not declared an attribute as filterable answers a filter on it with a 400
params.name: filters

exhaustiveNbHits.description: False when `nbHits` is an approximation, which Algolia does for very large result sets

hits.description: The matching records, in Algolia's ranked order. Each hit is the stored record itself — its attributes are this index's own content and are not knowable at build time — plus `objectID` and Algolia's `_highlightResult` annotations

objectID.description: The record's own id — what algolia-object-get, -save and -delete address it by

nbHits.description: How many records matched in total, which may exceed what this page returned

nbPages.description: How many pages the result set has at this `hitsPerPage`

page.description: The page that was returned, counting from 0

params.description: Echoes the search parameters Algolia actually applied, URL-encoded

processingTimeMS.description: How long Algolia spent on the query, in milliseconds

operations.description: Read one record from an index by its object id. Returns the stored record as it is; its attributes are this index's own content model, so nothing here can name them

params.description: The index the record is in, from algolia-index-list's `name` field
params.name: index_name

params.description: The record's own id — Algolia's `objectID`, from a search hit or from whatever wrote the record
params.name: object_id

response_schema.description: The stored record. Every attribute other than `objectID` is this index's own content and is not knowable at build time

objectID.description: The record's own id, echoed back

operations.description: Save one record at a known object id, creating it if it does not exist and REPLACING it wholesale if it does. This is not a partial update: attributes absent from the body are removed from the stored record. Algolia applies the write asynchronously, so the response's `taskID` is an acknowledgement of acceptance rather than of visibility, and a search run immediately afterwards may still return the old record

params.description: The index to write to, from algolia-index-list's `name` field. Algolia creates an index that does not exist on first write
params.name: index_name

params.description: The id to store the record under. An existing record at this id is replaced in full
params.name: object_id

schema.description: The record to store, as a flat or nested JSON object. Its attributes are this index's own content model and are not knowable at build time — see the header comment for why this is one opaque schema rather than named fields. An `objectID` inside the body is redundant with the one in the path and Algolia takes the path's

operations.repeatability_condition: the body carries the record's whole content as an absolute value rather than a delta, so re-sending it leaves the record in the state the caller asked for, however many times it runs. Conditional rather than idempotent because Algolia applies the write asynchronously and answers each call with a fresh `taskID`, so a stored result must never be served in place of running it

objectID.description: The id the record was stored under, echoed back

taskID.description: Algolia's own id for the asynchronous indexing task. The write is accepted when this returns and visible to search some time after; this connector declares no operation that waits on it

operations.description: Delete one record from an index by its object id. The record is gone with no undo route in the API — restoring it means re-indexing it from the source of truth. Algolia applies the delete asynchronously, so the `taskID` acknowledges acceptance rather than visibility

params.description: The index the record is in, from algolia-index-list's `name` field
params.name: index_name

params.description: The record's own id — Algolia's `objectID`. The record at this id is deleted
params.name: object_id

taskID.description: Algolia's own id for the asynchronous delete task. The delete is accepted when this returns and visible to search some time after
